metadata.explanation: Generate the customer resolution message with OpenAI.
Apply any subscription change required by the resolution.
Record the approved refund intent before billing changes.
Handle a billing failure during refund or credit.
Verify the customer identity before collecting further evidence.
Check for active incidents that affect refund policy.
Close the refund case once resolution is final.
Wait for a person to confirm or rewrite the customer message.
Choose the next capability from gathered evidence and guardrails.
Handle a failure sending the customer resolution message.
Load the payment and charge evidence for the refund.
Load the customer's subscription details for the case.
Load prior support history for this customer.
Load usage signals that may support or deny a refund.
Apply refund guardrails and set the recommended action.
Issue the refund through billing.
Close the loop when the agent cannot converge on an action.
Mark the case as not a refund request.
Offer account credit instead of a cash refund.
Prepare the resolution context and fallback customer message.
Re-check evidence after a capability returns to the decision loop.
Store the inbound refund request and open or reject the case.
Ask a human to approve or reject the recommended refund action.
Send the customer the message a person confirmed.
Store the customer message generated by OpenAI and open the confirmation gate.
Handle a subscription update failure after a resolution.
Use the deterministic customer message when OpenAI cannot confirm an answer.
Verify the billing outcome after a refund or credit.

diagnostics.message: attribute case-status is written by RPC ConfirmCustomerMessage, RPC EditCustomerMessage, Step AgentDecisionStep Execute, Step BillingFailedStep Execute, Step EmailFailedStep Execute, Step GuardrailStep Execute, Step IssueRefundStep Execute, Step NonConvergenceStep Execute, Step OfferAccountCreditStep Execute, Step ReCheckStep Execute, Step ReceiveRequestStep Execute, Step SendCustomerMessageStep Execute, Step StoreGeneratedCustomerMessageStep Execute, Step SubscriptionFailedStep Execute, Step UseFallbackCustomerMessageStep Execute, Step VerifyBillingStep Execute, and dexcli cannot prove that the writes are blind or share one exact registration lock; its definition declares no lock requirement. If these writes can run concurrently, declare dex.WritesRequireLock() or dex.WritesRequireAttributeLock and register that lock

attribute customer-message-draft is written by RPC EditCustomerMessage, Step StoreGeneratedCustomerMessageStep Execute, Step UseFallbackCustomerMessageStep Execute, and dexcli cannot prove that the writes are blind or share one exact registration lock; its definition declares no lock requirement. If these writes can run concurrently, declare dex.WritesRequireLock() or dex.WritesRequireAttributeLock and register that lock

attribute manager-rejection-reason is written by RPC RejectRefund, and dexcli cannot prove that the write is blind or protected by an exact registration lock; its definition declares no lock requirement. If these writes can run concurrently, declare dex.WritesRequireLock() or dex.WritesRequireAttributeLock and register that lock

group "failure" is neither one run of Steps that lead to each other nor one choice that a single Step makes; it falls into 3 parts: agenticNonConvergence; agenticNotARefund; agenticBillingFailed. Split it so that each group does one thing
